_note: What is at a major hub (where crews live) and a minor hub (where one or two rangers stay a night or two), how that differs by access, and what crews cost to run (Design tab, 'What's at a station'). basis: 'srr' = the SRR cost model's station item (an assumption set itself); 'published' = a public figure with its source; 'estimate' = ours, reasoning given. Replace with quotes. Salaries, field allowances and caretaker stipends are people costs: shown on their own line, not counted unless switched on (team rule).

options.name: Prefab station, about 60 m²: ops room, storage, bunks for 6
Two 20 ft containers: office and bunks for 4
Shared with an existing ranger post or partner (rent)
3.2 kW voice array, about 124 dB at 100 ft
Starlink Standard
options.note: Kit and $50/month in DRC (SRR sources); speeds are Starlink's typical residential range (25-220 down, 5-20 up), not a guarantee

kit.label: Medical cache, water purification, sensor spares, charging

crews.label: Most crews at a major hub
crews.note: Each major hub gets the crews its speakers need, up to this

salary_usd_yr.label: Loaded cost per person a year (shown, not counted)
salary_usd_yr.note: Local ranger pay; the Trades operations-staff estimate is $30k for network engineers

boat.label: Boat + 40 hp outboard (river sites)
boat.note: Price from the SRR access kit; life and fuel use are estimates

motor_share.label: Share of trip time under motor (the rest on foot)
motor_share.note: Trips mix boat or motorbike legs with walking to speakers off the river or road

field_days.label: Field days per ranger a year
field_days.note: About 1,600 working hours; leave, training and admin take the rest

team.label: Rangers per team in the field
team.note: Two for safety on the river and in the forest

day_h.label: Working hours in a field day

routine_yr.label: Routine visits per speaker a year

repair_yr.label: Repair visits per speaker a year (faults)
repair_yr.note: With health telemetry (TD-AUD-03) crews go only when a speaker reports a fault or misses its test

per_round.label: Speakers visited per round (one trip)
per_round.note: A crew strings nearby speakers into one round

fault_wait_d.label: Longest a speaker fault waits for a trip
fault_wait_d.note: A trip to the same place within this picks the fault up; otherwise it gets a repair trip of its own

work_days.label: Working days per stay at a minor hub
work_days.note: Three working days at the hub; travel days come on top

allowance_usd_night.label: Field allowance per ranger per night away
allowance_usd_night.note: Local per diem; a people cost like salaries

t_local_h.label: Day trip from a hub (one way, longest)
t_local_h.note: Speakers within 3 h of a hub are visited on day trips from it

t_day_h.label: Longest trip from a major hub to its minor hubs
t_day_h.note: 8 h: one day's travel; 12 h: a long day (default: the middle of the cost and time-away trade); 24 h: two days, with a night on the way

minor.label: Minor hub: an outstation where one or two rangers stay a night or two and work the speakers around it

options.name: Built shelter: 2 bunks, locked store, water filter
One 20 ft container: 2 bunks and store
Rented room at a health centre, school or mission
Starlink Mini
options.note: Kit price and a $50 monthly plan; check DRC availability

caretaker.label: Village caretaker at each minor hub (stipend)
caretaker.note: $30 a month: keeps the hub, checks nearby speakers after each monthly test and does simple repairs (resets, fuses, battery swaps); assumed to halve the routine visits and the faults that need a crew

access._note: What changes with the site's access (road, river, remote). Logistics multipliers are the SRR's (cost to haul and build).

river.name: Mooring, boat shed and fuel store
Raised floor above flood level
river.note: The river rises several metres in the wet season

remote.name: Six months of spares on site

how.road: Motorbikes; roads can close in the rainy season
how.river: Boat and outboard; fuel is the biggest running cost; sound and radio carry farther over water
how.remote: On foot or by canoe; everything carried in, longer stays because travel is the cost
